top.title: Takeaways from UH's win at West Virginia: Cougars bounce back, Keisean Henderson arrives
top.description: Houston Cougars wide receiver Amare Thomas (0) runs to the endzone for a touchdown after a catch against West Virginia Mountaineers during the first half of an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, in Morgantown, W.Va. (AP Photo/William Wotring) (William Wotring/Associated Press) MORGANTOWN, W.Va. - Five takeaways from No. 20 Houston's 34-31 victory over West Virginia on Saturday: Bounce-back win How would the Cougars respond after a disappointing performance in a 42-32 loss at Colorado ? The Cougars showed plenty of fight and, while the defense still showed some cracks and the offense sputtered at times, it was a Big 12 road win. UH also remains in position to reach the 10-win mark in consecutive seasons for the first time in program history. "We had to flush it out and come back stronger," running back Makhi Hughes said. "That's what we did." Look to the future All the talk has been about the Keisean Henderson era beginning in 2027. Well, that's still the case, but UH fans got a sneak peek when the true freshman made his first career start in place of injured fifth-year senior Conner Weigman . Henderson had some impressive moments (his 68-yard touchdown pass to Amare Thomas on the third play of the game) but it was what he didn't do that should be praised. The heralded freshman knew when to throw the ball away. He knew when not to try and do too much. He trusted his pass protection and had enough patience to stay in the pocket long enough to see things develop. He also showed his ability to run, including an 18-yard keeper. His game management down the stretch resembled that of a veteran, not a first-year quarterback who had been limited to 17 snaps all season. The future is bright for Henderson. Time to work UH's offensive line, a Joe Moore Award semifinalist for the best in the nation, gave Keisean Henderson plenty of time to work. Henderson averaged 3.19 seconds to throw on all dropbacks, according to Pro Football Focus. Only one of Henderson's two sacks was credited to the offensive line. "We got a couple of blitzes and got a little pressure on him, but outside of that, it was way too much time to throw the ball," West Virginia coach Rich Rodriguez said. We'll give the line a pass for the three false starts. Run, run, run That seems to be what the UH defense has seen in the past month. It was another heavy dose of runs Saturday as the Cougars allowed a season-high 329 yards to the Mountaineers. That followed the 249 yards allowed by UH in a double-digit loss at Colorado. In the first seven games this season, UH was among the best in the nation, allowing an average 82.6 yards per game. In the last four games, UH is allowing 241.5 points per game. The Boston Red Sox continue making changes to their roster, and their latest trade involves a pitcher who barely had an opportunity to contribute during the 2026 season. Boston traded right-hander Johan Oviedo to the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday in exchange for minor league left-hander Luke Dotson and a player to be named later or cash considerations. The move was part of a busy stretch for chief baseball officer Craig Breslow, who has already made several transactions as the organization prepares for the 2027 season. Oviedo's departure is particularly interesting because of the circumstances surrounding his brief time in Boston. The 28-year-old appeared in just one major league game for the Red Sox this season before an elbow injury essentially ended his year. Now, rather than bringing him back for another opportunity, Boston has decided to move in a different direction. Oviedo's Red Sox Tenure Never Got Started Oviedo arrived in Boston after previously pitching for the St. Louis Cardinals and Pittsburgh Pirates. He made 32 starts for Pittsburgh in 2023, posting a 4.31 ERA and demonstrating that he could handle a regular role in a major league rotation. The Red Sox have dealt Johan Oviedo to the Diamondbacks, per @ByRobertMurray. That’s a significant blow to their starting pitching depth, but he was out of options. https://t.co/b0b1dgH1DT — Tyler Milliken (@tylermilliken_) November 20, 2026 However, injuries interrupted his progress. Oviedo underwent Tommy John surgery and missed the entire 2024 season before returning during the following year. His opportunity with Boston proved similarly frustrating. The right-hander pitched 3 2/3 innings in relief against Houston on March 30 before being placed on the injured list with a right elbow strain. He eventually made a rehabilitation appearance for Triple-A Worcester in September but never returned to the major league mound for the Red Sox. That left Boston with limited opportunities to evaluate how Oviedo might fit into its future pitching plans. Arizona now gets the opportunity to determine whether he can regain his previous form. top.title: Colts revealed to have turned down great trade offer from Ravens for Daniel Jones
top.description: Colts revealed to have turned down great trade offer from Ravens for Daniel Jones originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indianapolis Colts managed to ship off a lot of players at the NFL trade deadline, but they notably didn't make a few other roster moves with Daniel Jones and Jonathan Taylor. Of the two, their star running back would've brought back the best return. But, since he's under contract beyond 2026, the Colts didn't have to move him. Jones, on the other hand, was released after Week 11, and clearly should've been traded. But, what could they have even got for Jones? According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, the Colts had a great trade offer on the table for Jones that they turned down in what's now very clearly a huge missed opportunity for the Colts. Colts trade offer they turned down from Ravens for Daniel Jones revealed "The Ravens offered the Colts a fourth-round draft pick for Daniel Jones and a fifth-round pick, with the condition that fifth-rounder would be returned to Indianapolis if Baltimore advanced to the playoffs," Schefter reports. "Minnesota also had interest in Jones. Indy held him, then released him." This is a brutal report from Schefter for the Colts. They had a chance to land a strong return for Jones that, at the very least, would've been a nice upgrade from the fifth to the fourth round. While that alone might not be worth trading a team's starting quarterback, in the Colts case, Jones only remained the starter for two games after that trade was declined by Indianapolis. MORE : Grading NFL trade deadline debuts, from Kirk Cousins' Vikings return to Josh Downs' impressive day There was a scenario where the Colts accept that trade, and the Ravens make the playoffs, and the Colts walk away with a fourth- and fifth-round pick for Jones, whom they would've released. Instead, the Colts didn't get anything for Jones, as they cut him one day after Thursday Night Football, and over one week after the NFL trade deadline had passed. It's about as clear of a missed trade opportunity as it can get. Combined with not trading Grover Stewart and Taylor despite solid offers being on the table, the Colts arguably made three big mistakes at this year's trade deadline. top.description: Celtics Suffer Stunning Collapse As Kings End Eight-Game Losing Streak originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Celtics couldn't have asked for a much better opportunity to end their losing streak Saturday night. Sacramento entered the game with one victory in its first 15 games, had lost eight consecutive contests and hadn't won at home all season. Boston still found a way to lose. Keegan Murray scored on a putback with five seconds remaining, lifting the Kings to a stunning 97-96 victory at Golden 1 Center. The Celtics led 54-41 at halftime and appeared positioned to take care of business against one of the NBA's struggling teams. Instead, Boston endured a disastrous third quarter that completely changed the game. The defeat was Boston's third consecutive loss and arguably its most frustrating of the season. Third-Quarter Disaster Changes Everything The Celtics controlled much of the first half despite playing without Jayson Tatum, Derrick White and Mitchell Robinson. Final Score https://t.co/7yfWfbrfgZ — Boston Celtics (@celtics) November 22, 2026 Boston opened the game with a 10-0 run and maintained a comfortable advantage entering halftime. Then everything changed. Sacramento outscored Boston 35-13 in the third quarter, turning a 13-point deficit into a nine-point lead. The Celtics missed all 13 of their three-point attempts during the period, an extraordinary shooting collapse that allowed the Kings to seize momentum. Boston finished the game shooting just 22% from beyond the arc despite attempting 58 three-pointers. Those numbers help explain how a team that appeared comfortably in control suddenly found itself fighting to avoid an embarrassing defeat. The Celtics eventually recovered enough to give themselves a chance in the final seconds. They just couldn't finish. top.description: Victor Wembanyama © X/ @spurs Victor Wembanyama produced another monster performance as the San Antonio Spurs blew out the New Orleans Pelicans 114-91 on Saturday. top.title: Former Real Madrid star urges Mourinho to hand more minutes to Carlos Espi: ‘He’s a problem solver’
top.description: Former Real Madrid star urges Mourinho to hand more minutes to Carlos Espi: ‘He’s a problem solver’ Speaking on COPE (h/t Defensa Central ), former Real Madrid goalkeeper Santi Canizares has urged Jose Mourinho to hand a greater role to young striker Carlos Espi. This comes after the summer arrival came up clutch for Los Blancos against Celta Vigo on Saturday, scoring the match-winning goal at the Santiago Bernabeu. Having come on as a substitute against the Galician outfit in the 79th minute, the 21-year-old Spaniard found the back of the net six minutes later to help Real Madrid secure a 2-1 win. Canizares wants a more prominent role for Espi Since joining Real Madrid from Levante last summer, Espi has had to settle for a secondary role, given that Kylian Mbappe has been the undisputed starter at centre-forward. In all, the towering striker has played only 62 minutes this season for the club, across 12 matches, but has chipped in with four goals already , which include three match-winners against Espanyol, Elche, and now Celta Vigo. Carlos Espi has excelled in his limited opportunities. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) And Canizares acknowledged that the youngster is unlikely to displace Mbappe from the starting line-up. However, he questioned why he could not receive more playing time in matches that are already under control. “He can’t be a starter because Mbappe is there, but there are many minutes in the second half where Madrid is winning 2-0 or 3-0 with half an hour left,” he said. “It would be fair for him to get more playing time, and there are ways to find it,” the former goalkeeper added. Canizares compares Espi to Joselu Canizares then went on to compare Espi with former Real Madrid striker Joselu, who also became known for his impact as a penalty-box striker from the bench. Real Madrid’s new super-sub. (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images) But the former shot-stopper believes that the 21-year-old is much better than the veteran forward, as he said: “For me, Carlos Espi is a much better striker than Joselu. Every goal he scores is worth points; he’s a problem solver, and it’s the worst thing that can happen to you if you’re winning against Madrid, when this player comes on.” Further highlighting the youngster’s attributes, he added: “Espi is a player who has everything, he can play in all systems and has the aura of Real Madrid, of epic moments.” Despite his admiration for Espi, Canizares was far less impressed with Real Madrid’s overall display against Celta. “Real Madrid weren’t a good team today; they only won thanks to the individual talent of their players,” he argued. “Real Madrid’s defensive system can’t handle the movement of the players in front of them,” he noted.

top.description: Elias Lindholm Delivers Historic Performance As Bruins Outlast Capitals originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Bruins needed Elias Lindholm to be good Saturday night. They probably weren't expecting him to deliver one of the most remarkable individual performances in franchise history. Lindholm scored four goals and added an assist as Boston defeated the Washington Capitals 7-5 at TD Garden. The veteran forward recorded his third career hat trick and first with the Bruins, finishing with a career-high five points. His four goals matched Boston's franchise record for goals in a single game. David Pastrnak added a goal and two assists, while Morgan Geekie and Charlie McAvoy each contributed three assists. Jeremy Swayman made 30 saves as the Bruins improved to 15-7-1 and earned their second consecutive victory. The performance was particularly meaningful for Lindholm, who has quietly become one of Boston's most important offensive contributors. Lindholm's Historic Night Creates Unusual Moment The Bruins trailed 1-0 when Lindholm scored his first goal on the power play midway through the opening period. He added another goal in the second period before completing his hat trick with a deflection that gave Boston a 5-4 advantage late in the frame. Hey Elias, how many you score tonight? https://t.co/XBXi1Y6XIV — Boston Bruins (@NHLBruins) November 22, 2026 What happened next was almost as memorable as the goal itself. Only one hat initially landed on the ice after Lindholm's third goal. Even Pastrnak later acknowledged that he hadn't immediately realized his teammate had completed a hat trick. The confusion didn't last long. Lindholm scored again early in the third period, redirecting another Pastrnak shot to extend Boston's lead to 6-4. This time, the crowd responded with considerably more enthusiasm. The fourth goal capped a remarkable night for a player whose contributions often extend beyond the scoresheet. top.title: Chelsea facing huge injury scare after Leeds United defeat
top.description: Chelsea facing huge injury scare after Leeds United defeat Moises Caicedo Injury Adds to Chelsea Problems After Leeds Defeat Chelsea have another problem to manage, and this one matters. Moises Caicedo went down early in the defeat to Leeds at Stamford Bridge, and Xabi Alonso admitted the club will need more time before understanding the full extent of the injury. The midfielder pulled up just after the 20-minute mark, with no obvious contact in the moment that ended his game. He received treatment and tried to continue, but was eventually replaced by Jordan Henderson. For a player who has already had fitness issues across the season, it is a worrying development. Caicedo setback hits Chelsea midfield Caicedo had only just returned after another physical concern on international duty. He asked to come off at half-time in Ecuador’s 2-0 win over Bolivia, yet was still cleared to start against Leeds. Early in the match he was involved in a series of heavy challenges and also needed treatment after landing awkwardly on his back. None of that helps the picture. Alonso was clear that Chelsea do not yet have answers. Instead, they have another wait, another assessment, and another key player in doubt at a point when the squad is already stretched. Photo IMAGO Xabi Alonso reacts to loss of momentum The timing mattered. Chelsea were still level when Caicedo went off, and for a while they looked in control. Emmanuel Emegha put them ahead, but Noah Okafor responded quickly. From there, Chelsea folded. Okafor added a second and Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted from the spot to seal a painful result. After the match, Alonso said: “It went wrong after the equaliser, after the change (with) Moi, we completely lost the momentum. Until then, we were doing okay, I think that we were creating, playing a lot on the pitch, we were coming out of the pressure. “But from that moment, they started believing and we started not believing. “And after that, we never got the good feeling mentality in any moment and we were not able to come for the pressure and we didn’t get close to their goal, so it completely changed.” Reece James and Maxence Lacroix latest That matters even more because Chelsea are already without Joao Pedro, Maxence Lacroix and Reece James. Alonso suggested Lacroix is closer to returning than James, saying: “I think that Max has a better chance than Reece. It’s not definitely that Reece won’t be back before then, but Max has a better chance.” Right now, Chelsea need clarity on Caicedo. Until they get it, the concern is obvious.

top.title: MotoGP Portuguese GP: Marc Marquez crowned 2026 champion as Marco Bezzecchi wins tense race
top.description: Motorsport photo Marc Marquez sealed the 2026 MotoGP title with a conservative ride to eighth at the Portuguese Grand Prix, as Marco Bezzecchi led a 1-2-3 finish for Aprilia. Having missed out on a chance to seal the title in both the Qatar Grand Prix and the Portimao sprint, Marquez only needed to finish inside the top nine on Sunday to secure the championship. While the Ducati rider led the race on the opening lap with a rapid getaway, he quickly dropped down the order, taking a safe approach following his surprise crash in Saturday’s contest. Although Bezzecchi recovered from a poor start to complete a double win at Portimao, with Jorge Martin finishing right behind second, it wasn’t enough to deny Marquez a title that had seemed inevitable since Martin’s crash at Phillip Island last month. Crossing the finish line in eighth, the Spaniard claimed his eighth MotoGP title, surpassing former rival Valentino Rossi and drawing level with Giacomo Agostini as the most successful rider in premier class history. Including his titles in the 125cc and 250cc categories, Marquez now has 10 world championships to his name, putting him third on the all-time list behind Agostini (15) and Angel Nieto (13). At the start of the race, Marquez made a brilliant launch from second on the grid, muscling past polesitter Bezzecchi to grab the lead. Bezzecchi, meanwhile, continued to tumble down the order on the opening lap, dropping as low as fifth as Raul Fernandez grabbed second. Meanwhile, Martin was on the move from seventh on the grid, jumping to fourth at the start before passing a recovering Bezzecchi under braking at the start of lap 2. This left three Aprilias chasing race leader Marquez, who had initially opened up a gap on the opening lap as his rivals fought among themselves. But the Ducati rider suddenly lost pace as the second lap began, with Fernandez, Martin and Bezzecchi all passing him in quick succession to establish an Aprilia 1-2-3. Among the three, Fernandez initially appeared as the quickest Aprilia, before Bezzecchi surged to the front, passing both Martin and Fernandez to take the lead on lap 15. Meanwhile, Marquez continued to drop down the order, losing further places to di Giannantonio, Ai Ogura and Brad Binder over the next 15 laps. This left him in ninth place - the minimum place he needed to secure to put the championship out of his rivals’ hands. As long as Martin was not winning the race, even a 14th place would have sufficed in their title battle. While Aprilia appeared to discuss manufacturer orders to orchestrate the result and keep Martin in the title fight, Bezzecchi was ultimately never asked to order position, having built a comfortable lead of three seconds. Bezzecchi went on to win the race with a comfortable margin to make it three victories in four races, with Martin taking the chequered flag in second after fending off a late attack from Fernandez. top.description: Photo by Alex Goodlett/Getty Images Victor Wembanyama revealed that, like the greats, including LeBron James, he was not going to think about the ethics of scoring 50 points in an NBA game. The 22-year-old went off for 50 points and 18 rebounds on an efficient 69% shooting from the field, while also contributing with 4 steals and 5 blocks. In his walkoff interview, the French centre said: “Unlike many of my peers, I’m not very good at stat padding.” It was believed that Wembanyama’s comments were a dig at Luka Doncic, who is the only other player to score 50+ points twice this season. However, in his press conference, he explained his statement by revealing what the greats of the game thought about this. “The greats they don’t think about that, I don’t think Lebron, Shai, Jokic, Luka, I don’t think they think about that. top.title: It Will Be Difficult To Stabilise What Tinubu Has Done If We Don’t Re-Elect Him — Wike
top.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said that denying President Bola Tinubu a second term will amount to abandoning and undermining the positive effects of the various economic reforms and other policies his administration has started to implement. Wike argued that though the removal of fuel subsidy came with initial difficulties, it would be in the best interest of Nigeria and its people for the President to complete the foundation he has laid for the country’s recovery and prosperity. He spoke on Sunday during a thanksgiving and dedication service at St. Peter’s Anglican Church, Rumueprikom, his hometown in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State, where the Rainbow Coalition campaign council was dedicated ahead of the 2027 general elections. Wike Wike, who said the campaigns would begin on November 23, described Tinubu as a courageous leader who took difficult decisions to prevent Nigeria from collapsing. “This country was on the verge of collapse, on the verge of collapse, but by the grace of God, He gave us somebody who is courageous,” the former governor said. The minister cited the relative stability in the university system, saying lecturers’ strikes over unpaid entitlements, which previously disrupted academic calendars, are no longer a recurring problem under the Tinubu administration. He also recalled the difficulties pensioners faced in securing their payments, arguing that the President’s decisions were necessary to address the country’s challenges. Wike described the removal of the fuel subsidy as one such difficult decision, acknowledging it came with disadvantages but insisting the challenges were temporary. “Now, in doing that, there must be some disadvantages. “And that’s why they say these disadvantages will be temporarily seen. As he has laid his foundation, now it’s time for prosperity,” he said. “If we don’t re-elect him, then it will be difficult to stabilise what he has done,” he said. The minister called on Christians, Muslims and traditional worshippers to support the re-election bid, insisting that the campaign would not discriminate on religious grounds. “I am not a native doctor, but I need their votes now. I need everybody’s votes because I know they are registered voters,” he added. “The Muslims, I need their votes too. The Christians like you, we need your votes.” Wike also defended the Tinubu administration against claims of religious imbalance in its appointments, saying Christians benefited more from the government than under previous administrations. “Since Nigeria was created, we have never had the kind of appointments that are going on in this country now,” said the minister. He further urged the congregation to participate actively in the forthcoming elections, warning that those who refuse to vote would have to live with the consequences of decisions made by others. “If you don’t participate, and you have a bad leader, it will also affect you,” he added. nigeria.title: Atiku’s aide challenges Tinubu over prosperity promise
nigeria.description: A media aide to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Paul Ibe, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to provide evidence of economic improvements under his administration, saying Nigerians need tangible results rather than assurances of future prosperity. Ibe made the remarks in a post on his X handle on Sunday while reacting to Tinubu’s message in Ibadan that Nigeria was on the path to prosperity. He argued that Nigerians needed to see improvements in their living conditions, particularly in the cost of food, transportation, electricity and other essential services. According to him, the President should explain the achievements of his administration and how its policies have translated into better living conditions for citizens, especially as he seeks another term in 2027. Ibe questioned how long households would have to contend with rising living expenses, while workers struggle with increasing costs and businesses face energy-related challenges. He maintained that government claims of economic progress should be assessed against the everyday experiences of Nigerians. On the reported agreement to reopen a vehicle assembly plant, Ibe said productive investment was welcome but argued that its benefits should be measured by the actual resumption of operations, employment opportunities and wider economic impact. He also acknowledged the importance of infrastructure development, while stressing that government should equally account for its impact on the livelihoods of citizens. Ibe further questioned the emphasis on future generations in the President’s appeal for Nigerians to remain committed to the administration’s policies, saying the immediate needs of children and struggling households should also receive attention. He called on the Federal Government to provide Nigerians with a clear account of the outcomes of the sacrifices associated with its policies, including the benefits recorded and when households could expect meaningful relief. Reacting to Tinubu’s remarks about the opposition, Ibe said opposition parties had a legitimate role in scrutinising the administration’s performance, while citizens were entitled to consider alternative political positions. He argued that public confidence in government should be strengthened through responses to citizens’ concerns and demonstrable improvements in their living conditions. Ibe said the benefits of prosperity should be reflected in household purchasing power, workers’ wages, the survival of businesses and the security of communities. He maintained that the administration should provide evidence of its achievements and address the economic and security concerns confronting Nigerians. nigeria.title: Emir of Daura trends on X after tourist’s ‘inappropriate touching’ allegation
nigeria.description: The Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, has become a subject of controversy on X after a female tourist accused him of touching her inappropriately during a visit to his palace in Katsina State. The allegation followed the circulation of a video on social media which appears to show the traditional ruler interacting with the tourist during her visit. The woman, who identifies herself online as ‘beduina’, made the allegation in an Instagram post after completing a 30-day trip across different parts of Nigeria. She said the incident occurred on Saturday, November 14, when she visited the Emir’s palace in Daura. Recounting the encounter, the tourist said she was taken into an elegant room, where she sat with the traditional ruler and engaged in a conversation. She alleged that the Emir held her hand and began playing with it before hugging and kissing her on the cheek. According to her, the encounter took a disturbing turn when the traditional ruler allegedly touched her breasts. “That was a shock for me. I told him ‘emir no, no, no, no’, ‘emir you cannot be touching’, but he was just laughing about it,” she wrote. The tourist said she was particularly disturbed that the alleged incident happened inside a palace, despite having travelled through different parts of Nigeria without experiencing sexual assault in public spaces. “I wasn’t sexually assaulted at any moment when walking through streets of Nigeria, even in busy crowded places, but to my shock I was assaulted in a palace by a traditional leader who should be behaving in exemplary and dignified way,” she said. nigeria.title: NAFDAC destroys N22.73bn fake, unsafe products, records 52 arrests
nigeria.description: … 821 seizures, 179 premises shut in eight months By Chioma Obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has destroyed unwholesome products valued at approximately N22.73 billion, seized 821 products and secured 52 arrests in eight months as it intensified enforcement against unsafe and substandard regulated products. The agency disclosed that it carried out 5,542 enforcement activities, including 213 raids, between January and August 2026, while 179 premises were shut and 221 sanctions imposed. The figures formed part of major regulatory milestones presented by NAFDAC at the International Pharmaceutical Regulators Programme (IPRP) Management Committee Meeting in Prague, Czech Republic, held from November 18 to 19, 2026. The agency also reported progress in local pharmaceutical manufacturing, disclosing that more than 70 per cent of finished pharmaceutical products covered by its 5+5 policy and Ceiling 36 are now being manufactured in Nigeria. The development is expected to reduce dependence on imported medicines and strengthen the country’s medicine security. In its regulatory update, NAFDAC said it had sustained its World Health Organisation (WHO) Maturity Level 3 status and was working towards attaining Maturity Level 4, the highest level of the WHO Global Benchmarking Tool. It identified digital innovation as a critical component of the transition, citing the Integrated Regulatory Information Management System (IRIMS), Performance Management System (i-PMS), GMP Inspection (GMPi), Application and AI-assisted Technical Screening Tools (TST), and the revised Med Safety App. The revised application is designed to strengthen the reporting of adverse drug reactions and substandard and falsified medical products. NAFDAC also highlighted Nigeria’s growing influence in African pharmaceutical regulation, noting that it had emerged as a reference National Regulatory Authority, hosting regulatory authorities from Uganda, The Gambia, Mozambique and Côte d’Ivoire for technical capacity building and institutional benchmarking. Another milestone was Nigeria’s ratification of the African Medicines Agency (AMA) Treaty, with the instruments of ratification deposited on October 25, 2026. The agency said the achievements reflected the strategic leadership of its Director-General, Prof. Mojisola Christianah Adeyeye, and ongoing efforts to strengthen institutional capacity, promote science-based regulation and deepen international regulatory cooperation. NAFDAC reaffirmed its commitment to protecting public health, strengthening Nigeria’s pharmaceutical industry and positioning the country as a leading regulatory authority in Africa. Atiku said the tragedy, which claimed several lives, highlighted the risks faced by millions of Nigerians who rely on boats for daily transportation, particularly in riverine communities, and called for urgent government action to protect them. In a statement on Sunday, the Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Kola Ologbondiyan, described the incident as a heartbreaking tragedy that had plunged the affected communities into mourning. He said the victims were travelling to honour a departed loved one when the accident occurred. “What makes this tragedy even more painful is that these were ordinary Nigerians who set out in love and solidarity to honour a departed loved one, only to meet their own untimely deaths on the waters,” Ologbondiyan said. “Bayelsa has lost fathers, mothers, children and breadwinners. He, however, called for a thorough investigation into the cause of the mishap and stricter enforcement of regulations against boat overloading, the use of unseaworthy vessels and other unsafe practices. nigeria.title: Nigerian sentenced to 24 months in US prison over COVID-19 relief fraud
nigeria.description: A Nigerian man, Chukwuebuka Arinze, has been sentenced to two years in prison in the United States for using another person’s identity to fraudulently apply for COVID-19 relief funds. Arinze, 38, was convicted of aggravated identity theft after using a farmer’s Social Security number to submit an application under the US government’s Coronavirus Food Assistance Program. He was sentenced on October 30, 2026, by US District Judge Robert Rossiter Jr. at a federal court in Omaha, Nebraska, according to the US Attorney’s Office for the District of Nebraska. The Nigerian will also serve one year of supervised release after his imprisonment and face deportation from the United States, the statement said. Prosecutors said Arinze, who was living outside the US at the time, sent an email to the Farm Service Agency office in Wayne, Nebraska, on September 28, 2020, seeking financial assistance under the programme. The email, titled “CFAP Forms,” contained an application for the second phase of the Coronavirus Food Assistance Program, known as CFAP2, alongside an Automated Clearing House payment form. Both documents were submitted in the name of a dairy farmer identified in court records as Victim 1 and contained the farmer’s Social Security number. The US authorities said Arinze knowingly used the identification number belonging to the farmer without authorisation to validate the application. He was later brought to the United States to face prosecution over the offence. The Coronavirus Food Assistance Program was established by the US Department of Agriculture during the COVID-19 pandemic to support agricultural producers affected by declining sales and rising marketing costs. The initiative was administered through the department’s Farm Service Agency and Agricultural Marketing Service. Its first phase ran from May 26 to September 11, 2020, while the second phase, CFAP2, opened from September 21 to December 11 of the same year. The programme allowed applicants to self-certify their eligibility without submitting evidence of pandemic-related business losses. The Federal Bureau of Investigation investigated the case. nigeria.description: Agency intercepts 160 explosives bound for Zamfara, seizes 4.6 tonnes of cannabis in Osun By Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arrested a 37-year-old South African professional golfer, Grobler Henlo, and a 25-year-old Kenyan chef, Abubakar Faiza Njambi, over an alleged attempt to smuggle 50.40 kilogrammes of Loud, a potent strain of cannabis, into Nigeria. Further examination revealed that tracking devices had been installed in the travelling boxes and on his mobile phone, a development the agency said was similar to what was discovered in the bags abandoned by the American basketball player a month later. entertainment.description: Have you ever spent six hours in an airport waiting for your connecting flight, watching the departure screens, browsing duty-free shops and wondering what the city outside looks like? Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. These are important considerations, but there is another question worth asking: What else can this ticket give me? I am talking about stopovers, not the hurried two-hour connection where you are running between terminals, but an intentional break in your journey that allows you to experience another destination before continuing to the country you originally planned to visit. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. First, Understand What You Are Booking A layover is generally a connection between flights; a stopover is a longer, planned break in your journey. Airlines define these differently, and the distinction matters because some offer special hotel packages, sightseeing tours or complimentary accommodation to qualifying passengers. For example, imagine travelling from Lagos to London through Istanbul. Instead of spending a few hours at Istanbul Airport, you could investigate whether your ticket qualifies for a longer stopover, allowing you to explore Istanbul before continuing to London. You have now turned one international journey into an opportunity to experience two destinations outside Nigeria. The secret is to investigate the stopover before purchasing your ticket, rather than arriving at the airport and hoping the airline will allow you to stay longer. For visa purposes, Nigerians do not qualify, but with a valid Turkish visa you would be able to qualify for some of the perks. Under the standard programme, eligible Economy Class passengers can receive one night in a four-star hotel, while Business Class passengers may receive two nights in a five-star or boutique hotel. entertainment.title: Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada
entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. That position follows a strong 2025, when TCL reported, based on Omdia data, a 31.1% share of global Mini LED TV shipments and 118.0% year on year shipment growth. entertainment.title: A Safari, a Beach & Easy Entry? 5 African Spots for Your Christmas Holiday
entertainment.description: Five African destinations Nigerian passport holders can visit visa-free or with visa on arrival this Christmas holiday. Image: AI-generated. The group chat has the concerts, the dinners and the Detty December link-ups covered. But has anyone planned the getaway? Beyond the usual Lagos parties and end-of-year outings, there is a whole continent waiting to be explored, with sun-soaked beaches, wildlife safaris, exciting food scenes and cities with plenty of stories to tell. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Whether you are travelling solo, gathering your friends, taking the family along or joining a curated travel group, here are five destinations worth considering for your Christmas holiday. Kenya Imagine spotting lions and giraffes against a city skyline before breakfast, then catching an evening flight or train straight to the coast for fresh seafood by the Indian Ocean. That contrast is what makes Kenya such a rewarding December escape. Nairobi gives you immediate access to wildlife at Nairobi National Park and the Giraffe Centre alongside lively restaurants and art spaces in Westlands and Karen, while longer itineraries open up classic game drives in the Maasai Mara, views of Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli, and warm beach days in Diani or Watamu. Nigerian citizens enjoy visa-free entry for short stays of up to 60 days without needing a paid eTA, leaving more room in your budget for safaris and coastal stays. Rwanda Not everyone wants their year-end holiday to feel like a non-stop sprint, and Rwanda is built for travellers who prefer scenery, clean air, and an unhurried pace. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. entertainment.title: Visa Report Identifies Opportunity to Integrate Digital Payments with SMEs Business Operations in Nigeria
entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). The Indianapolis Colts managed to ship off a lot of players at the NFL trade deadline, but they notably didn't make a few other roster moves with Daniel Jones and Jonathan Taylor. sports.description: Check out the Brazil women's team's schedule for friendlies in Japan The Brazil Women's National Team will wrap up their 2026 schedule with two friendlies in Japan against the hosts. In April 2012, in the Kirin Challenge Cup, Japan won again, this time 4–1 at Kobe Wing Stadium in Kobe. The friendly in Hiroshima will therefore be the teams' third meeting on Japanese soil. technology.title: Come for the science, stay for the big iron: Supercomputer admin on why he loves the job
technology.description: Web hosting might seem like an unlikely on-ramp to supercomputer administration, but it set Mark O'Shea on his way to running some of Australia's most powerful machines. O'Shea is team leader for supercomputing operations and senior supercomputing systems administrator at Australia's Pawsey Supercomputing Research Centre . Pawsey is home to Setonix, an HPE Cray EX supercomputer with more than 200,000 AMD EPYC CPU cores and hundreds of AMD Instinct MI250X accelerators. Its GPU partition ranks 87th in the November TOP500 and 37th in the Green500 , which measures computational performance per watt. "Working in web hosting wasn't much different to what I was doing a few years later with supercomputers," O'Shea tells The Register . "Datacenters are essentially several thousand computers, as are supercomputers. "So, we essentially had the same problems," he says, especially as regards cooling and power management. There's no single formal route into supercomputer administration in Australia, O'Shea says. He picked up the necessary skills over time. Andrew Underwood, Dell's chief technology officer for high-performance computing and artificial intelligence across the Asia-Pacific, Japan, and China, says that lack of formal training means some supercomputer admins start in academia. He's observed that many HPC admins emerge from the sciences, catching the computing bug during their studies. A biologist working with a massive genomics database, for example, might discover a taste for running the systems behind it. "The biologist might decide they want to be someone working in IT helping other biologists transform their industry," Underwood says . "One of the things I really admire about people who work in the supercomputing field is they take it so seriously," Underwood adds. "It's almost a passion, a hobby, more so than it is a job." "They want to play that real supporting and foundational role of assisting and engaging with scientists to help them use the technology to solve the problems the world faces." O'Shea agrees, noting that many people who get into supercomputer admin are PhD graduates who stick around their universities after they graduate. Some of them gravitate toward running the departmental computers and then wind up in supercomputing. "There are many roles around universities allowing people to be introduced to [supercomputer administration] while still doing enterprise-style or more departmental admin for researchers and system administration," O'Shea says. Regardless of how a supercomputer admin gets their gig, both O'Shea and Underwood say the supersysadmin community is tight knit – which may not always be a good thing. "As an industry in supercomputing, we need to be open to people from diverse backgrounds," Underwood says, "and we need to build these frameworks like the Student Cluster Competition, conferences like eResearch and the SC Conference, where students can get educated and systems admins get exposed to continual training." science.title: 10 things that worry me about chasing the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt
science.description: null On Aug. 2, 2027, I'll be in Luxor, Egypt, to witness what could be the greatest total solar eclipse of my life. I've seen nine total solar eclipses across the world, but this one promises to be different. For a remarkable six minutes and 22 seconds, the moon will completely cover the sun, plunging Egypt's ancient temples and monuments into eerie twilight as the solar corona bursts into view. I've been calling it the "eclipse of the century" for many years, and for good reason. It will be the longest total solar eclipse until 2114 — and the longest on land of the 21st century — and it will take place in one of the most extraordinary places on Earth. What could go wrong? I've chased eclipses long enough to know that the celestial mechanics are the easy part. The moon will arrive exactly on schedule — that's guaranteed. Everything else — the weather, the crowds, the transport, the equipment and the people — is rather less predictable. From the possibility of dust storms to uncertainty about whether boats will even be allowed to move on the Nile, there are plenty of reasons to be slightly wary about what awaits eclipse chasers after the ultimate bragging rights on Aug. 2, 2027. Here are the 10 things worrying me most about the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt. A dust storm could make the eclipsed sun less impressive. (Image credit: Grant Faint via Getty Images) 1. A sudden dust storm The chances of cloud-free skies in Luxor and anywhere in Upper Egypt in August are exceptionally high — close to 100%. That's almost unheard of in eclipse-chasing. However, clouds aren't the only thing that can obscure the sun. Dust and sand are potential hazards in the Egyptian desert, and a dust storm at the wrong moment could affect—though probably not ruin—the view. Although the sun will almost certainly be visible during the eclipse, airborne dust could hide the delicate structure of the solar corona. 2. Chaos in Luxor How many people will descend on Luxor for the eclipse? August is normally a quiet month for tourism in Luxor because of the oppressive heat. In 2027, however, the city and its surrounding urban area — population about four million — could swell as eclipse chasers, tour groups, photographers and curious visitors descend. Hotels, roads, buses and archaeological sites will all face extraordinary pressure. My biggest concern isn't necessarily the number of people watching the eclipse, but the logistical chaos it will create. Let's take Mallorca as an example for the 2026 eclipse. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch. science.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. But the company had never attempted a Ship catch, which is a taller order, given how much faster and farther Starship upper stages fly. So snagging Ship on the first try was a very big deal, according to Musk. "Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," he told Baker and Gracias on Wednesday. The Ship upper stage of SpaceX's Starship megarocket comes back to its launch tower for a "chopsticks" catch on Nov. 14, 2026, during the vehicle's 15th test flight. (Image credit: SpaceX) And SpaceX is very serious about Starship reuse. Musk has said that the company wants to launch about 10,000 Starship missions per year by 2030. science.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
science.description: null Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the solar system's innermost planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Today's orbital insertion is the latest milestone in BepiColombo's Mercury arrival phase, which is expected to take about six months in total. Arrival began on Sept. 3, when the MTM released MPO and Mio. The two orbiters remain connected today; they won't separate until Dec. 9 or thereabouts. Shortly thereafter, Mio will settle into its final orbit, a highly elliptical path that will take it over Mercury's poles. MPO is also destined for a polar orbit, though a much less elliptical one than Mio's; the ESA probe will conduct a series of engine burns before finally getting there on March 10, 2027. BepiColombo won't start doing science work until April 6, 2027. The two probes will gather complementary data from their two different vantage points, shedding a great deal of light on a mysterious world. "The mission will study all aspects of Mercury, from the structure and dynamics of its magnetosphere and how it interacts with the solar wind , to its internal structure with its large iron core, and the origin of the planet’s magnetic field," ESA officials wrote in a BepiColombo mission description . "The data will enable scientists to understand more about the origin and evolution of a planet located close to its parent star, and a better understanding of the overall evolution of our solar system," they added.

The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on Nov. 20, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX ended its launch webcast just after that touchdown, so we didn't get to see the Falcon 9's upper stage power its way to orbit. USSF-317 is a classified mission, so we don't know what the upper stage is carrying or where exactly it's headed. However, some experts think that USSF-317 may be hauling a batch of SpaceX's Starshield satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO) for the Space Force's Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio, which helps the military keep tabs on potential targets around the world. The Falcon 9's first stage rests on the deck of a drone ship after launching the USSF-317 mission. The vast majority of this year's Falcon 9 missions — about 70% of them — have been devoted to building out SpaceX's Starlink LEO internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 satellites. The Falcon 9 has been putting up incredible numbers lately — it flew a whopping 165 times in 2025 , for example — but the workhorse rocket is on its way out . SpaceX plans to retire both it and the Falcon Heavy in favor of its fully reusable Starship megarocket, which deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites on its most recent two test flights .

science.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental?
science.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. Effectively, he came upon a formula that could make sense of primes’ seemingly random appearances among numbers. science.description: null On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station. Today, the I nternational Space Station is about the size of a football field and typically hosts up to seven crewmembers. But back in 1998, it was a pretty tight squeeze. A Russian Proton rocket launches the core Zarya module of the International Space Station (left), which can be seen in orbit (right) during the first mission to the station in 1998. (Image credit: NASA/Roscosmos) Why it mattered As of this writing, the International Space Station is 28 years old, and has seen steady rotating crews of astronauts since the year 2000 (for 26 years and counting). It is a marvel of space engineering, but every engineering marvel begins the same: with the first piece. And that is what the Zarya module is: The foundation of the International Space Station. Zarya, also known as the Functional Cargo Block (or Russian acronym FGB), is the core module of the space station around which every other module was attached. It weighed 42,600 pounds at launch and is just aver 41 feet long and 13.5 feet wide. Inside, it boasts a total habitable volume of 1,650 cubic feet. science.title: Don't turn the moon into the Wild West, scientists warn
science.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.

Awards to small businesses around the country are addressing some of NASA’s most crucial technology needs for exploration of the Moon and Mars while fueling the U.S. space economy. NASA’s Small Business Innovation Research/Small Business Technology Transfer (SBIR/STTR) program recently selected 302 innovative projects, for a total investment of up to $171 million in seed funding. This early-stage research and development work will tackle an array of topics, including those related to Artemis and the establishment of a U.S. Moon Base . Selected projects include next-generation battery solutions, robotic systems with sensing capabilities for the extreme lunar environment, and tools to prepare for construction of critical infrastructure, such as lunar landing pads. NASA’s SBIR/STTR program provides support for entrepreneurs, startups, and small businesses to advance and commercialize technologies that can advance the agency’s missions. Working with the program, a company’s path toward commercialization or infusion into NASA missions occurs in phases. The latest awards involved two of these phases. The new Phase I contracts will receive up to $225,000 each to establish the merit and feasibility of their proposed innovation. A portion of the projects selected are STTR awards, provided to small businesses partnered with research institutions. The Phase II awards, with 98 contracts valued at up to $1.3 million each, will continue work begun in Phase I projects selected in 2025, targeting demonstration and delivery of the innovative technologies. Following are a few examples of research supported through these recent awards: Bringing Power to Moon and Mars An SBIR Phase II award for Opterus Research and Development Inc. supports a project focused on bringing power to the surface of the Moon and Mars by developing a modular system of rollable solar arrays. The arrays can be handled robotically, are compatible with various support structures, and work even in dusty surface conditions. The technology could be scaled up to 50 kilowatts, and it could provide a reliable power source to help both NASA and commercial space companies develop infrastructure on the Moon .
